headline: High: shared git-repo writes make prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; Great Expectations' local-only posture limits external exfiltration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and shares state via a shared git repo, so attacker-controlled content in files can be re-ingested as instructions. great_expectations also reads/writes files for validation results and documentation, creating a plausible file-based bridge. No MCP or clipboard bridge is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace files
IF Aider is prompted to summarize or edit content that Great Expectations wrote into shared files
mitigations: Separate the agents into different working directories
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files into prompts
Review shared files before either agent processes them
Use read-only mounts for Great Expectations outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files and reject untrusted instruction-like text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys, while Great Expectations is documented as network-egress none. If they share a workspace, sensitive source code or validation artifacts can flow into Aider and then to third-party model providers. Great Expectations alone does not exfiltrate, but the pair still creates a default leakage path through Aider.
conditions: IF shared files contain secrets, source code, or regulated data
IF Aider sends those contents to configured model providers
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared repo
Use separate repos for code and validation artifacts
Redact sensitive fields before Aider reads files
Restrict Aider to a local-only model backend
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on prompts and file reads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem, execute shell, and modify git state; its shared_state_with_other_instances is via a shared git repo. Great Expectations also reads/writes files for validation outputs. Concurrent edits to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git state, and no locking is documented. This is a direct overlap in default write surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git repository
IF either agent runs without external locking or branch isolation
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Serialize writes with a manual lock file
Run Great Expectations in a separate output directory
Commit after each Aider change before GE runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate or edit code and git history, and Great Expectations can consume files and produce validation results. If GE treats Aider-authored artifacts as authoritative without a review step, bad code or bad assumptions can cascade into incorrect validation or downstream actions. The pair is not documented as autonomous action-taking, so high is not justified.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes files produced by Aider without human review
IF validation results are used to gate merges or releases
mitigations: Insert a manual review step before validation runs
Require tests to fail closed on schema changes
Compare validation outputs against a known baseline
Keep Aider edits on a feature branch until reviewed
requires-engineering: add provenance checks for Aider-generated artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and may send content to configured model providers, while Great Expectations is local-only network-wise and touches validation results/documentation. The pair can create policy mismatch if regulated data is placed in shared files, but no specific residency or certification conflict is documented in either profile. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same files.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repository
IF Aider is configured to send that data to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo
Use a DPA-approved local model for Aider
Separate compliance-sensitive artifacts from code
Document retention rules for validation outputs
requires-engineering: map data classes to approved processing locations
